title: How Freemasons Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain Freemasonry: a recent split in Boise, Idaho, where Crispin Hertog (spelled as heard) founded a secular Practice Lodge aligned with the Grand Orient of France and was expelled from Boise Lodge number two; competing origin theories (King Solomon's Temple legend with Hiram Abiff and the "Mahabone" word, Knights Templar, operative stonemason trade guilds, Druids, Egyptian cults); the shift from operative to speculative Freemasons; Elizabeth Aldworth; the 1717 Grand Lodge of London; York, Scottish and French rites; American Freemasonry and Founding Fathers; Masonic symbolism on the dollar bill; Boston Tea Party theory; initiation rituals, membership requirements, lodge officers; alleged penalties for revealing secrets; the Illuminati and Adam Weishaupt; Washington D.C. ley line theories; the anti-Masonic movement after William Morgan's 1826 disappearance; famous Freemasons; Prince Hall Freemasonry. Ends with a listener email from a former prison guard's child about Attica prison, and a promo for a trivia tour and SXSW panel vote.

segments.title: Opening banter and promos
segments.summary: Hosts promote a SXSW PanelPicker vote and an upcoming all-star trivia tour starting in Atlanta in October, then transition into the Freemasons topic.

segments.title: Boise Practice Lodge controversy
segments.summary: Crispin Hertog was summoned to Boise Lodge number two of the Grand Lodge of Idaho after founding the secular Practice Lodge aligned with the Grand Orient of France, which allows discussion of religion and politics and does not require belief in a supreme being. He was expelled, not for sharing secrets.

segments.title: Origins of Freemasons: legends and theories
segments.summary: The hosts describe competing origin theories: ancient Druids and Egyptian Isis-Osiris cults, and the King Solomon's Temple legend in which master mason Hiram Abiff was killed and the word Mahabone became the secret password for the third degree. They also cover the Knights Templar theory.

segments.title: Stonemason guilds to speculative lodges
segments.summary: Operative stonemasons and rough masons are distinguished; trade guilds formed lodges that evolved secret handshakes and passwords. Lodges later admitted speculative members such as artists and aristocrats, and the group developed Enlightenment-era philosophy and religious tolerance. The 1717 Grand Lodge of London and James Anderson's constitution are mentioned, and the story of Elizabeth Aldworth is told alongside reasons for excluding women. Women's auxiliaries such as the Order of the Amaranth and Order of the Eastern Star are noted.

segments.title: American Freemasonry and Founding Fathers
segments.summary: Freemasonry's influence in America, including George Washington, Benjamin Franklin and several signers of the Declaration and Constitution. The Masonic pyramid-and-eye on the dollar bill is explained through Mitch Horowitz's reading. Theories about the Boston Tea Party are discussed as unproven. After the Revolution, American lodges separated from provincial lodges, and the York and Scottish Rites are contrasted.

segments.title: Membership, beliefs and initiation
segments.summary: Discussion of religion within Freemasonry: belief in a supreme being called the Grand Architect and oaths on a sacred volume, the ban on discussing religion and politics in meetings, and the membership process of two sponsors, a secret ballot vote, dues and philanthropy. Initiation rituals involving a mock death and rebirth as Hiram Abiff are described.

segments.title: Alleged penalties, degrees and the great name
segments.summary: Alleged penalties for revealing secrets (tongue, heart, bowels, top of skull) are described as speculation the Masons deny. The name of the Grand Architect, said to be Yabulon, is explained as combining Yahweh, Baal and Osiris. Favorite degrees and the thirty-three degree structure are mentioned.

segments.title: Lodge officers and Masonic symbols
segments.summary: Typical lodge officers are listed, including master, senior and junior wardens, treasurer, secretary, deacons, inner guard, chaplain, director of ceremonies and organist. The square and compass with the G are explained as standing for God or geometry, and the square and compass boundaries.

segments.title: Illuminati and Washington D.C. ley line theories
segments.summary: Adam Weishaupt's Illuminati and their alleged alliance with Bavarian Masons, which ended after the government ordered the Illuminati to disband. Ley line theories about Washington D.C. street layout and the Washington Obelisk are presented as unfounded.

segments.title: Anti-Masonic movement and William Morgan
segments.summary: The anti-Masonic movement followed William Morgan's disappearance after he published Freemasonry Exposed in 1826. Accounts of his abduction to the Niagara River are described as uncertain, and New York lodge numbers dropped sharply. The movement faded after the Civil War.

segments.title: Famous Freemasons and Prince Hall
segments.summary: The hosts list famous Freemasons including Henry Clay, Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Mark Twain and John Wayne. They note Prince Hall Freemasonry and Masonic support for abolition, and Masonic persecution during the Holocaust.

segments.title: Listener mail on Attica prison
segments.summary: A listener whose father was a correctional officer at Attica describes prison life and guard stress, followed by a sign-off promo for the website.
